_help.about: Techniques (design 30 Sept §BO–§BP): verbs learned from peoples, permanent and weightless. taught_by lists people ids (data/peoples). player_can: the player performs it in the world; otherwise it is a camp thing that raises the camp's ceilings. first_to_build marks the one to implement first. Restart after editing.
_help.category: light | fire | fuel | food | water | materials | shelter | marks | travel
_help.params: Numbers the engine reads for the techniques built as verbs (fishing_line, coppice, resin_torch, ember_carrier, fat_lamp): first guesses by Claude Code 1 Oct, the designer owns them. ember_game_h: a live coal lasts this many game hours in the carrier before it goes cold. fat_lamp burn_game_h: the lamp burns this long once lit. kind (fatwood, candlenut): the torch.json kinds entry the technique makes, and genera, where that kind's plant must grow (design §CQ, not wired). relights_torch (ember_carrier): the coal can be blown into an unlit torch (torch.json ember_relight, §CQ, not wired).

techniques.name: Resin torch
techniques.verb: dip a cattail head or bark twist in pine pitch
techniques.unlocks: a torch that burns longer and brighter and shrugs off drizzle (torch.json resin block)

techniques.name: Fatwood
techniques.verb: split resin-soaked heartwood out of an old pine stump
techniques.unlocks: fatwood splints: a hot, long-burning torch found not made

techniques.name: Ember carrier
techniques.verb: wrap a live coal in tinder fungus or punk wood and bark
techniques.unlocks: carry fire for a day or more with no light; lay a new fire from it, or blow it into a torch that went out (§CQ); it goes cold if neglected (fire is never made, only carried)

techniques.name: Fat lamp
techniques.verb: a stone bowl, rendered fat, a moss wick
techniques.unlocks: a dim light that burns for hours and won't blow out; set it down inside a shelter

techniques.name: Candlenuts
techniques.verb: string oil-rich nuts on a rib; they burn one after another
techniques.unlocks: a small, slow tropical light: a small circle that burns long (torch.json kinds candlenut, §CQ)

techniques.name: Peat cutting
techniques.verb: cut peat in bricks, stack it to dry over summer
techniques.unlocks: a slow smoky fuel harvested, not chopped; a camp's fuel without a forest

techniques.name: Dung fires
techniques.verb: gather and dry herd dung
techniques.unlocks: fuel where there are no trees; depends on the animals, which depend on the grass

techniques.name: Charcoal burning
techniques.verb: stack wood in a mound, seal it with turf, burn it slow for days
techniques.unlocks: charcoal: hotter than any wood; what the marsh bloomery needs (exchange)

techniques.name: Coppicing
techniques.verb: cut hazel or ash to the stump; it throws straight poles again in seven years
techniques.unlocks: a woodlot that is a fuel crop, no clearing; the fix for the restraint rule

techniques.name: Pitch and tar
techniques.verb: cook pine resin or birch bark in a pot
techniques.unlocks: glue for the spear, tar for boats and torches

techniques.name: The weir
techniques.verb: drive stakes in a V at the tideline or across a river; the tide or the current leaves fish behind it
techniques.unlocks: a camp's fish_run ceiling; the player can build one at a suitable shore

techniques.name: Line and hook
techniques.verb: twist a line, carve a hook of bone or shell, cut a pole
techniques.unlocks: fish with a pole and line, the patient way; the spear stays the fast way

techniques.name: Clam garden
techniques.verb: wall a beach terrace at the low-tide line; clams thrive in the flat behind it
techniques.unlocks: a shellfish crop that needs no seed

techniques.name: Salt pans
techniques.verb: seawater or brine in a shallow rock pan; the sun does the work
techniques.unlocks: salt: food keeps; the coast's trade good inland

techniques.name: Drying and smoking
techniques.verb: racks in the wind, or over a slow smoky fire
techniques.unlocks: fish and meat keep through the lean season; the first storage

techniques.name: Flood-plain crop
techniques.verb: plant on the silt the flood leaves
techniques.unlocks: the river's crop ceiling: fertiliser delivered every year

techniques.name: Digging stick
techniques.verb: a fire-hardened stick: dig tubers, plant tubers, cut a channel
techniques.unlocks: plant and dig; irrigate a plot from a stream (irrigation is a rule: a plot near water or a channel counts as watered)

techniques.name: Channel
techniques.verb: cut a ditch from a stream to a plot (a qanat where it is dry)
techniques.unlocks: a plot away from the bank is watered; the ditch visibly carries water, no fluid physics

techniques.name: Terracing
techniques.verb: step a slope so the soil stays and the water walks down
techniques.unlocks: crops on a hillside; terraces gone to bramble read as ridges (ruin)

techniques.name: Swidden
techniques.verb: clear a garden-sized patch, burn it, plant in the ash, walk away in a few years and let the forest close
techniques.unlocks: the rainforest's crop; sustainable small, deadly big (restraint)

techniques.name: Black earth
techniques.verb: charcoal, bone and broken pots worked into poor soil for generations
techniques.unlocks: soil that stays rich; a ruin that grows better than the land around it

techniques.name: Forest garden
techniques.verb: plant useful trees wherever you camp
techniques.unlocks: groves of nut and palm cluster on old village sites; the forest remembers

techniques.name: Chuño
techniques.verb: freeze potatoes on cold nights, tread the water out, dry them in the sun
techniques.unlocks: food that keeps for years; the highland's storage

techniques.name: The burn
techniques.verb: burn the old grass in season; new growth comes back sweet and the game follows it
techniques.unlocks: grassland stays grassland; fire-followers bloom; the grassland's farming (wildfire.json rules)

techniques.name: The herd
techniques.verb: follow, then keep, the animals: goats, cattle, reindeer, llamas
techniques.unlocks: fuel and food where nothing can be planted; built last
techniques.note: expensive: animals that move and breed

techniques.name: Wild rice
techniques.verb: bend the stalks over the canoe and knock the grain in
techniques.unlocks: a lake crop nobody planted

techniques.name: Floating garden
techniques.verb: build a garden bed on the water from reeds and mud
techniques.unlocks: chinampas: a crop on the lake

techniques.name: Fishpond
techniques.verb: wall a pond on the reef or the tide flat
techniques.unlocks: fish kept alive until wanted

techniques.name: Honey
techniques.verb: smoke a wild hive, take the comb
techniques.unlocks: the sweetest thing in the world; the mangrove's trade good

techniques.name: Water from sand
techniques.verb: a reed pushed into damp sand, sucked; water carried in ostrich eggshells
techniques.unlocks: drink where there is no river

techniques.name: Qanat
techniques.verb: a tunnel from a hillside spring, carried underground so it does not evaporate
techniques.unlocks: a desert camp's water and its plots

techniques.name: The lined spring
techniques.verb: line a spring with stones so it stays clean
techniques.unlocks: the one fixed thing on the grassland; every band comes back to it

techniques.name: Cave water
techniques.verb: the water is all underground; find the cave pool
techniques.unlocks: a karst camp's water

techniques.retired: §EH (5 Oct, Mike): no metal in Torchfire 1; kept as a row so old references resolve, never taught, never shown
techniques.name: Bog iron
techniques.verb: rake iron lumps out of the marsh, roast them in a clay bloomery packed with charcoal, hammer the sponge clean
techniques.unlocks: the only metal in the world; a place, not a tech level; the bog regrows its iron over decades

techniques.name: Reed building
techniques.verb: bundle reeds into pillars and arches; thatch, mats, boats
techniques.unlocks: a house of reed

techniques.name: Trackway
techniques.verb: lay split timber across the bog
techniques.unlocks: cross a marsh dry-footed; the bog preserves it

techniques.name: Pottery
techniques.verb: dig riverbank clay, throw a pot, fire it in a domed kiln of clay and brush
techniques.unlocks: storage: the hinge of the ladder; the kiln hump is the ruin

techniques.name: Knapping
techniques.verb: strike flakes off obsidian or flint
techniques.unlocks: a knife: dress carcasses, cut cordage; the knapping floor glitters for ten thousand years

techniques.name: Lime
techniques.verb: burn limestone in a kiln; slake it with water
techniques.unlocks: mortar, plaster and whitewash: a hut becomes a house

techniques.name: Dry-stone walling
techniques.verb: fit stones without mortar so well they stand five hundred years
techniques.unlocks: walls and terraces; ridges under the moss when they fall

techniques.name: Cordage and baskets
techniques.verb: twist grass or bark fibre into rope; coil and weave baskets
techniques.unlocks: carry more (burden); snares, nets, lines

techniques.name: Hide
techniques.verb: scrape, smoke and sew with sinew and a bone needle
techniques.unlocks: every warm thing to wear; shelter skins

techniques.name: Ochre
techniques.verb: grind red and yellow iron earth on a stone, mix it with fat
techniques.unlocks: paint, sunscreen, insect repellent, hide cure; mark your own trail beside the forgotten waymarks

techniques.name: Birch bark
techniques.verb: peel bark in sheets; sew containers and canoes; tinder fungus off the trunk
techniques.unlocks: containers, a canoe, the ember carrier's wrap

techniques.name: Snow and sod
techniques.verb: build from snow blocks, sod, whalebone and driftwood
techniques.unlocks: shelter where there are no trees; the lamp is the hearth

techniques.name: Stilt house
techniques.verb: a platform on poles over the tide; boats for streets
techniques.unlocks: a house over the water

techniques.name: Reed boat
techniques.verb: bundle reeds into a hull
techniques.unlocks: cross the lake; a boat to fish from
techniques.note: the spec's boats stay a someday; this is a camp craft first

techniques.name: Fire is carried, never made
techniques.verb: every flame is borrowed from a hearth; the only new fire is lightning
techniques.unlocks: the hearth economy's law (§AW–§AX); no fire drill exists

techniques.name: Mud and stone
techniques.verb: puddle clay with straw and water, lay it in courses or bricks on a stone footing, plaster it; roof with poles and brush and a hand of mud
techniques.unlocks: the camp's storage rung and its rooms; wall stubs and a melted mound are the ruin

techniques.name: Ichu torch
techniques.verb: twist a bundle of dry ichu grass tight, bind it with a grass cord, light it at the hearth
techniques.unlocks: a short bright torch made from any tussock; burns fast and dies in the wind

techniques.name: The cistern
techniques.verb: cut a bottle-shaped hole in the soft rock, plaster it with lime, apron the mouth so the rain runs in
techniques.unlocks: a camp with no cenote holds through the dry season; the ceiling rises above a handful; a dry cistern keeps nuts and grain

techniques.name: Nixtamal
techniques.verb: soak maize in limewater (or wood-ash lye) overnight, rinse, hull, grind
techniques.unlocks: maize counts as a full staple for the player and the camp; without it maize is half a meal

techniques.name: Cane torch
techniques.verb: bind dry cane, reed or bamboo in a bundle and light one end
techniques.unlocks: a bright, fast-burning torch from reeds or bamboo; its charred stub marks rock: the karst folk's waymark inside a cave

techniques.name: Fishing torch
techniques.verb: split the end of a pole and wedge in strips of birch bark (a twist of dry reed where there is no birch); stand it upright in the bow so the flame hangs out over the water
techniques.unlocks: a torch that lights the shallows from a boat or a pile at night; fish come to the light and can be speared

techniques.name: Oysters off the roots
techniques.verb: at low tide, from the boat, cut the oysters off the stilt roots with a knife: the oyster, never the root
techniques.unlocks: the player gathers oysters and cockles at low tide in any tidal forest

techniques.name: Eel trap
techniques.verb: weave a long basket of willow withies or reed with a funnel mouth; set it in a channel, mouth downstream, on a dark autumn night
techniques.unlocks: the camp's fish_run ceiling; the player can set a trap in a marsh channel

techniques.name: Fir candle
techniques.verb: dig the resin-black pine root out of the peat face, dry it by the fire, split it into thin splinters a forearm long, stand one in a split stick
techniques.unlocks: a hot bright splint for inside the reed house, found at the peat face; a bundle sees out an evening

techniques.name: The goat herd
techniques.verb: follow the wild goats, then keep them: a fold of dry stone, the kids brought in, the milkers kept and the young males eaten
techniques.unlocks: the camp's herd ceiling: milk and cheese, dung for the fire above the trees, tallow for the light (built last in the engine)

techniques.name: Rushlight
techniques.verb: peel a rush from the spring's edge to its pith, draw it through melted tallow, wedge it in a split stick
techniques.unlocks: a short, cheap light to set down inside a shelter; any rendered fat serves, and the herd's tallow makes it by the handful

techniques.name: The Three Sisters
techniques.verb: maize, beans and squash in one mound: the stalk holds the bean up, the bean feeds the soil, the squash leaf shades out the weeds
techniques.unlocks: the forest's crop ceiling: corn braided under the roof, a pit of nuts, then the specialist

techniques.name: Clay lamp
techniques.verb: a fired saucer with a pinched spout; fat or oil in the dish, a twist of rush laid in the spout; lit from the hearth
techniques.unlocks: a lamp to set down inside a shelter: dim, hours, will not blow out; the potter makes the dish and the player fills and lights it

techniques.name: The thorn fence
techniques.verb: cut acacia or thorn brush and stack it in a ring, cut ends in; the gap is closed at dusk with one more bush
techniques.unlocks: the camp's night: a boma around herd, hearth and houses; the pen's dung is its fuel and, in time, its midden

techniques.name: Acorn leaching
techniques.verb: dry and crack the acorns, grind them on the bedrock mortar, spread the meal in a basin scooped in sand and pour water through until it stops running brown
techniques.unlocks: acorn meal: the scrub's storage crop, a year in the granary; the mortar holes are the ruin

techniques.name: Fire-stick
techniques.verb: a twist of cured grass or a dry thorn branch lit at the hearth and carried burning at arm's length
techniques.unlocks: a fast torch that burns out in minutes; dropped lit in cured grass in a dry spell it starts a fire (wildfire.json)

techniques.name: Stone cache
techniques.verb: pile fitted stones over meat and fish on the permafrost so fox and bear cannot get in; the cold does the rest
techniques.unlocks: food keeps through the dark; the player can cache food under stones and come back for it

techniques.name: Stone figure
techniques.verb: stack stones into a figure that reads at a distance: this way, a cache here, the crossing is there
techniques.unlocks: the player can raise a waymark that persists and reads along the road

techniques.name: Reading the crown
techniques.verb: loop a vine round the trunk and your waist, cut footholds, whip the loop up as you climb; in the crown read the tree: which branch fruits, which hollow hums, which nest is within reach, which bromeliad tank is sweet; take part and come down slow
techniques.unlocks: the player harvests fruit, eggs, comb and water in the crown of any giant tree; a giant reads as a larder

techniques.name: Vine bridge
techniques.verb: twist liana or hardy-kiwi vine into cables as thick as an arm, anchor them round two trunks, hang a floor of cross-poles and walk it in; rebuild it every third year, before it rots
techniques.unlocks: the player crosses their bridges; taught, lashes a short one between two close trees (a gap, not a gorge)

techniques.name: Rope ladder
techniques.verb: two bast ropes, bamboo rungs lashed a forearm apart, coiled at the platform lip and let down; hauled up at dusk
techniques.unlocks: once the headman has met you their ladders come down for you; the player can hang one from a platform or a thick branch

techniques.name: Living root bridge
techniques.verb: plant a rubber fig on each bank, lead its aerial roots across a hollowed palm trunk or a bamboo, twist them, tie them, wait: fifteen to thirty years before it bears a person, and it grows stronger every year after
techniques.unlocks: the camp's crossing that never rots; the ruin's one signature that grows

techniques.name: Tree platform
techniques.verb: pick a giant with a crotch 8–15 m up, lash a frame of poles into it with rattan, prop it from below with four to ten poles, floor it with bark or split bamboo, roof it with leaf
techniques.unlocks: the camp's shelter: one family per giant, the village the size of the stand

techniques.name: Hearth box
techniques.verb: a box of poles floored with a hand of clay and a bed of sand, set on the platform; the fire lives in it and never touches the floor; if the clay cracks, the folk cut the box loose and let it fall
techniques.unlocks: the player lays a fire on a platform, a bridge-head or a big branch without burning it; the ember comes up in a bark bundle

techniques.name: Dammar torch
techniques.verb: knock the hardened resin off the bark where a dipterocarp has bled, pound it and pack it into a leaf or bark tube or a split bamboo, light it at the hearth box
techniques.unlocks: the dammar torch: a slow bright hand light in the wet forests; fir pitch is the temperate stand-in

techniques._help_id: Added by Claude Code, 5 Oct: the id the code learns it by (Techniques.knows("fire_arrow")). While camp is OPEN the teacher is the headman of the people's camp at the end of the opening road (a placeholder until the designer names the camp: put a people id or a camp key in camp).
techniques.name: Fire arrow
techniques.camp: OPEN — which camp teaches it is undecided (§ED.7)
techniques.effect: a drawn arrow may be lit at any flame; it lights what it hits
